subject: Orchard Health — AZ1 network isolation causing elevated 5xx & latency
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@orchardhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Orchard Health Ops <ops@orchardhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 09:12:48 -0700
Subject: Latency spike + 502s from our US-WEST customers (AZ1)

Connor —

We're seeing a sharp increase in 502/5xx errors and median latency jumping from ~80ms to 1.2s for requests routed to the US-WEST AZ1 cluster starting ~09:05 PDT. Impacting search and document ingestion for our live customers. Our dashboards show a sudden climb in error rate and a drop in KV cache hit rate for requests that landed in AZ1.

We filed an internal ops ticket (OPS-913) but wanted to escalate because this is affecting checkout flows for multiple customers. Can Redwood confirm whether there is a regional networking issue or routing mis-spray? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether you can steer traffic away from AZ1.

Attachments: orchard_5xx-spike-09-12.png (screenshot of Grafana), orchard-kvcache-stats-09-25.log (recent KV stats)

— Samantha
Samantha Lee
VP Product, Orchard Health
Samantha's mobile: +1 (415) 555-0163
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@orchardhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 09:18:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike + 502s from our US-WEST customers (AZ1)

Samantha —

Thanks for the heads up and the attachments. I'm escalating immediately. Short answers: 1) We see elevated 5xx and latency correlated with a network flapping event in AZ1 that started ~09:03 PDT; 2) We can initiate a cross-region reroute (US-WEST2 / US-EAST fallback) for your tenant to restore service within minutes, and 3) we'll open an exec bridge with infra and networking.

Next steps I'm starting now:
- Opening priority bridge and pinging infra/networking (cc'd Soojin & Marissa)
- Drafting a brief comm to your team with recommended traffic steering and expected impact
- Confirming whether Orchard wants an immediate cross-region steer or to attempt localized mitigating ops first

I'll be on the bridge and will update you every 15 min.

— Connor
Connor O'Brien
AM, Customer Reliability 
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 09:22:05 -07:00
Subject: RE: Latency spike + 502s from our US-WEST customers (AZ1)

On Thu, May 30, 2029 at 09:18, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Soojin & Marissa — Connor's escalated this. We see the same telemetry.

Joining bridge now. Quick telemetry notes:
- AZ1 edge nodes show intermittent 502 bursts with upstream timeouts to the KV cache tier.
- KV cache miss rate jumped 18% -> 62% for sequence-length 128 workloads (matches customer's traffic).
- Network interface error counters (eni) on a subset of AZ1 hosts spiked at 09:02:40 and haven't fully recovered.

Initial mitigation options (ranked):
1) Immediate per-tenant cross-region steer to US-WEST2 (fast, small consistency window, recommended).
2) Auto-scaling additional KV cache read-only replicas in AZ1 (risky while ENI unstable).
3) Route-level retries with longer timeouts (temporary, can increase cost/latency).

I recommend option 1 for Orchard. I'll prepare the steer and a rollback plan. Requesting exec approval for a brief traffic diversion (expected <10% of total US-WEST traffic to be rerouted for Orchard).

Attachments: diagnostic snippet attached to bridge notes.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 09:30:10 -07:00
Subject: RE: Latency spike + 502s from our US-WEST customers (AZ1)

Looping in Rishi for executive authorization & credits decision and flagging this for the on-call exec.

Rishi — quick summary: Orchard (large healthcare customer, production checkout impacts) is experiencing region-level network flapping in US-WEST AZ1 that has caused KV cache misses and a spike in 5xx. SRE recommends immediate per-tenant cross-region steer to US-WEST2. Expected customer impact: transient increased token latency during redirect and potential short-lived duplicate requests. Estimated time to apply steer and validate: ~8–12 minutes.

Please reply with approval to proceed and any guidance on customer-facing credits/compassion.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 09:34:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike + 502s from our US-WEST customers (AZ1)

Approved — proceed with the per-tenant steer to US-WEST2. Keep me on the bridge and capture a short exec note for the customer. If Orchard escalates to their C-suite, I'll join the customer call.

Also: pre-approve a one-time goodwill credit up to $12k if Orchard requests it (CC finance later). We should avoid overcommitting until we have post-incident numbers, but give the CS team the green light for an initial gesture if the outage lasts >2 hours.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@orchardhealth.com>, Orchard Health Ops <ops@orchardhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 09:46:55 -07:00
Subject: Orchard Health — immediate steer to US-WEST2 applied; monitoring

Samantha —

Action taken: per your approval we applied a per-tenant traffic steer so new requests are routed to US-WEST2. Rollout completed at 09:45 PDT. Early validation: error rate for your tenant is down ~94% (5xx), median latency back to ~95ms for sampled requests. We will continue monitoring for 60 minutes and then sample a promoted traffic window back to AZ1 if stable.

What to expect:
- Short-lived increased latency for in-flight requests (few hundred ms) during the redirect window.
- Session affinity keys might briefly miss; we recommend clients retry idempotently for ingestion flows.
- We'll continue to investigate root cause in AZ1 and share a post-mortem.

Attachments: RMP-authorization-request.pdf (authorization for steer)

Please confirm you are seeing traffic normalization on your side. If you want us to keep steer active longer, say the word and we'll hold it while we complete the full validation.

— Connor
Connor O'Brien
AM, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@orchardhealth.com>

Cc: Jason Park <jason.park@orchardhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 15:42:09 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchard Health — immediate steer to US-WEST2 applied; monitoring

Connor / team —

Thanks for the rapid response and the brief. Confirming Orchard saw error rates return to normal after ~09:50 PDT and checkout flows recovered. Our internal monitoring aligns with your numbers. We'll keep the steer in place until you provide a root cause and rollback plan.

Requesting the post-incident report include: timeline of events, root cause (ENI vs infra control plane), whether any data loss or degraded consistency occurred for ingestion, and recommended safeguards to prevent recurrence (per-tenant circuit-breaker or preferred-region pinning).

We'll schedule a follow-up for tomorrow 11:00 PDT for the post-mortem review. Appreciate the one-time goodwill credit pre-approval — we'll discuss after the post-mortem.

— Samantha
Samantha Lee
VP Product, Orchard Health
